summary: Former fire lookout on the summit of Clark Peak in the Pinaleno Mountains, Coronado NF; listed as gone, with remnants reported around the top.

facts.status_note: Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the tower as gone; the Mountain Field Guide reports remnants of the lookout's history around the top

access.note: Hikers reach the mountain's vicinity from Forest Road 803 by Clark Peak Trail #301 and a short summit spur

visit.trail_note: Clark Peak Trail #301 from Forest Road 803, then a short summit spur

events.note: Peakbagging.com lists 'Clark Peak (LO site)' on the 1972 Webb Peak map; in its table an LO site is one where the building has been removed, or the status is unknown

evidence.supports: summit is a forested 9,011-foot peak in the Pinaleno Mountains, part of the Coronado NF southwest of Safford
evidence.quote: Clark Peak is a forested 9,011-foot summit in southeastern Arizona’s Pinaleño Mountains

evidence.supports: the summit is part of the Coronado National Forest, southwest of Safford
evidence.quote: part of the Coronado National Forest southwest of Safford

evidence.supports: an old fire lookout once occupied the summit; remnants of its history can still be found around the top
evidence.quote: An old fire lookout once occupied the summit, and remnants of its history can still be found around the top.

evidence.supports: hikers reach the vicinity via Forest Road 803 and Clark Peak Trail #301, then a short summit spur
evidence.quote: hikers can reach the vicinity of the mountain using Forest Road 803 and Clark Peak Trail #301, followed by a short summit spur.

evidence.supports: LiDAR places the summit at about 9,010.9 ft
evidence.quote: Modern LiDAR measurements place Clark Peak at approximately 9,010.9 feet
Older maps and references commonly give an elevation of about 9,006 feet

evidence.supports: Peakbagging lists Clark Peak as a lookout site (LO site), on the Webb Peak map of 1972
the table's LO site label means the building has been removed, or its status is unknown
evidence.quote: where the building has been removed and there may be no evidence remaining, or it's status may be unknown

evidence.supports: Clark Peak in Graham County; type Tower; status Gone

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Mountain Field Guide gives about 9,010.9 ft from LiDAR and about 9,006 ft from older maps. The record's elevation_m is still null; the summit is about 2,745 m on either figure.

notes_for_editor: No source I read gives a build date, design, staffing or removal date for the Clark Peak lookout. The Forest Lookouts page for Clark Peak (westlookouts.weebly.com/clark-peak.html) gives only the forest name. The Peakbagging row and the FFLA entry agree on place and gone status. The Peakbagging row's Webb Peak map and 1972 year were checked against the table text on the page; the quote in evidence covers only the site name. A search result mentioned a 1996 Clark Peak Fire that started near Riggs Lake, not on the summit; no source I read ties it to the lookout, so it is left out. The Forest Service trail page for Trail #301 returned 404 when I tried it. No photos added.
